7364.t: From κάμηλος (kắmēlos, “camel”) + πάρδαλις (pắrdălĭs, “leopard”); from the fact that a giraffe has a long neck like a camel and is spotted like a leopard.

7388.t: From καταγελάω (kătăgelắō, “to mock; to jeer”), from κατα- (kătă-, “against”) + γελάω (gelắō, “to laugh at”).

7366.t: Possibly an Old Iranian borrowing, from Proto-Iranian *kamarā- (“something curved”), from *kamárati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kmárati, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kh₂em- (“to bend, curve”).

7328.t: Formation like θύρσος (thúrsos). An expression of the Dionysiac religion, and as such suspected of foreign origin: probably Pre-Greek, in spite of older interpretations in Indo-European terms.

7367.t: κάρπασος (kárpăsos) [from the Hebrew כַּרְפַּס (karpás, “a type of expensive fabric made of cotton”)] + -ινος (-inos)

7340.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kā́r. No suitable Indo-European root exists, therefore the source is probably Pre-Greek.

7305.t: From θλάω (thláō, “I crush, I bruise”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

7318.t: Probably related to θύον (thúon, “cypress-pine”). The two words could be derived from θύω (thúō, “to burn”) but this is not clear.

7323.t: Traditionally taken as a derivative in -μο- (-mo-) from θύω (thúō, “to smoke”), though Beekes is skeptical of this theory and notes that "[a]s a local plant name, the word is liable to be of Pre-Greek origin".

7338.t: Probably from the same root as κέλομαι (kélomai) and κελεύω (keleúō, “to urge, command”), that is, Proto-Indo-European *kel- (“to drive”); however, the -θ- (-th-) is difficult to explain morphologically.

7304.t: Perhaps inherited from Proto-Indo-European *dʰi-né-ǵʰ-ti ~ *dʰi-n-ǵʰ-énti, a nasal-infix present from *dʰeyǵʰ- (“to mold”), with supposed parallels in Latin fingō (“to shape; feign”) and Old Armenian դիզանեմ (dizanem, “to heap up, gather”).

7320.t: Traditionally derived from an o-grade of Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to put”), the same root of τίθημι (títhēmi, “to put, place, set”), as "the settled penalty".

7371.t: From κάρος (kắros, “heavy sleep, torpor”) + -όω (-óō, verbal suffix).

7380.t: From the root of καθίστημι (kathístēmi) + -σις (-sis); also analyzable as κατα- (kata-) + στάσις (stásis).
